change: BootOrder lists entry B before entry A, written in a preparation boot; entry B holds a second signed loader
wrong_if: The prediction is wrong if the boot does not continue, or if the first boot option the firmware tries is not Boot0003, entry B.
It is wrong if the first differing event is not the measurement of BootOrder (event 14), or if that measurement does not carry the digest of the order as it was written.
It is wrong if any register besides 1 and 4 differs, if register 4 does not differ, or if the image digest logged is not the second loader's.
not_scored: UEFI 2.11 (3.3 Globally Defined Variables, PDF page 165) says BootCurrent names the boot option that was selected for the current boot, so it should read 0003, the number of entry B. The loader does not read that variable, and it is not kept in the variable store file, so no recording shows it and no row covers it.

Entry A is not expected to be tried at all: the loader behind entry B never returns to the firmware. UEFI 2.11 (3.1.1 Boot Manager Programming, PDF page 153) speaks of the next option only for an option that comes back. The rows on events and on refusal lines would show a second attempt, but 'A was not tried' is not a field of its own.

In the normal run the firmware measures the Boot#### variables in the order BootOrder lists them (events 15 to 18). With the changed order the measurements of Boot0003 and Boot0002 are expected to exchange places. A comparison pairs events by register, type and digest wherever they stand, so this exchange is not visible in any field and is not a row.

boot_order.form: entry B holds a second loader, signed with the same key

rows.reason: The firmware must use the stored boot order for a normal boot, and the order now starts with entry B, an active boot option whose loader is signed with the enrolled db key, like the loader the normal run accepts from entry A.
BootOrder is an ordered list whose first element is the first option to try, and it now starts with 0003.
rows.note: UEFI describes no console message; the lines are this firmware's own. So this row only asks that the first line that differs from the normal run names Boot0003.

rows.expect: BdsDxe: loading Boot0003 "Lux entry B" from \EFI\LUX\B.EFI
rows.reason: The normal run's first line names Boot0002, the label 'Lux entry A' and the path of A.EFI, and the same line with entry B's number, label and path is expected.
The line that names the option being loaded is the first console line of the normal run.
The normal run gives up no boot option, and entry B's loader is as acceptable as entry A's.

The cited text lets the firmware add boot options to the list and remove invalid ones, and in the normal run this firmware measured the order exactly as the preparation boot had written it, so the same is expected here.
rows.note: The same text guarantees a change only after the next reset; the order is written in a preparation boot and the machine is switched off before the recorded boot. The predicted digest is the SHA-256 of the eight bytes that will be written as BootOrder (03 00 02 00 00 00 01 00). In the normal run the digest of event 14 is the SHA-256 of the variable's value, which the agreement gate recomputed.

rows.reason: Events 1 to 13 of the normal run measure the firmware, the Secure Boot variables and platform configuration, none of which the boot order touches, and event 14 is the measurement of BootOrder.
Event 14 of the normal run carries stop 5.
rows.note: The stop is this project's own label for an event, not a specification term.

The measurement of the original order and the digest of the loader behind entry A, which is not started, exist only in the normal run.
The measurement of the changed order and the digest of the second loader, at the place where the normal run has the first loader's (event 28), exist only in the changed run.

rows.note: The least certain row. The memory map does react to boot options: the two-entry normal run differs from the plain normal run from line 12 of the report. The map is whatever the firmware hands over, and nothing fixes it.
